Memory mapping, access width, ordering, atomicity and locking rules for reading or updating the status words.
Positions and masks of UV2 event word one bits below forty and of generation four event word two positions beyond accelerator flag four.

findings.text: UV2 event word one dedicates ten successive positions starting at bit forty to group one TLB completion signals numbered six through fifteen, each position having its own one-hot mask.
UV2 event word one places real time interval expiry at bit fifty and broadcast dashboard signalling at bit fifty one, each as an independent single-bit flag with a one-hot mask.

Generic external IO line zero position and mask are generation sensitive, present as bit one on generation five systems and reported as absent otherwise through a zero mask and a negative shift marker. Selection uses predicate is_uv with tag UV5, so consumers must branch on generation before shifting.

Event word one is modelled as a sixty four bit container readable either as one plain whole word or through five alternative single-bit field overlays corresponding to a common view and to generations five, four, three and two.

Common and generation five overlays share an identical lower arrangement of thirty eight signals: interprocessor notice, four external IO lines, profiler, broadcast data, general processor flag, six crossbar TLB lines, then twenty four remote directory TLB lines, with the upper twenty six bits reserved.

Generation four overlay starts with profiler, broadcast data and general processor flags, continues with twenty four group zero TLB lines followed by twenty four group one TLB lines, leaving the top thirteen bits reserved.

Generation three and generation two overlays share one arrangement: broadcast data, power management request, sixteen message accelerator lines, sixteen group zero TLB lines, sixteen group one TLB lines, real time interval and broadcast dashboard flags, with the top twelve bits reserved.
The alias for event word one is at offset 0x70088 and event word two is at offset 0x70100.

Common event word two arranges real time interval at bit zero, broadcast dashboard at bit one, then thirty two real time comparator flags numbered zero to thirty one at bits two through thirty three, each as a single-bit flag with a one-hot mask.

Generation four event word two begins with message accelerator completion flags zero through four at bits zero through four, each single-bit with a one-hot mask; the lane header advertises many further accelerator, interval, dashboard and comparator positions whose bodies are absent from this fragment.

Every documented event indicator in the overlays is a one-bit readable writable field packed in increasing order from the least significant end, with a reserved field filling the remainder to the full word width.

A negative shift value signals absence rather than a usable position and must never feed a shift operation; reserved upper bits in every overlay carry no defined meaning and must be masked or preserved on update.
